title: Distributed E2EE semantic WebRTC streaming with AI-Snake negotiated compute contracts
goal: Extend Ananta Pair-Dev from encrypted view-state deltas into an optional semantic media mode. Participants negotiate compute contribution, reconstruction delay, validators and short-lived task masters. The Hub/SFU coordinates signalling, routing and opaque contracts without needing plaintext media in strict E2EE mode.

codebase_alignment.pair_view_architecture: docs/architecture/pair-view-sync.md already defines minimal encrypted deltas, WebRTC DataChannel or Hub Relay selection, snapshot recovery, payload limits and default-deny control.
codebase_alignment.pair_view_types: frontend-angular/src/app/services/pair-view-sync.types.ts is the current typed wire contract and must remain backward compatible.
codebase_alignment.ai_snake_learning: docs/operator-tui/ai-snake-heuristic-evolution.md already implements observation, candidate validation, simulation, shadow run, progressive rollout, quarantine and rollback. Reuse this lifecycle.
codebase_alignment.ai_snake_config: agent/routes/ai_snake_config.py only persists registered schema keys. New settings must be added through chat_setting_definitions rather than arbitrary JSON.
codebase_alignment.worker_contracts: agent/services/worker_contract_service.py already models capabilities, routing decisions and normalized contracts. Reuse terminology where useful, but keep real-time peer leases separate from background worker jobs.
known_gaps: Pair-View is currently documented as n=2 only.
Current view sync transports UI state, not semantic scene graphs, residual image tiles or media recovery data.
Current permission keys do not cover compute contribution, semantic processing, validator or temporary master roles.
The Hub relay forwards opaque payloads and must remain unable to inspect plaintext under strict E2EE.

principles: AI-Snake explains and proposes; deterministic policy validates and commits.
No permanent global master. Mastership is short-lived and task-scoped.
Audio and urgent interaction events are never delayed by the configurable 2-20 second reconstruction window.
Every client may refuse compute contribution or force ordinary encrypted WebRTC fallback.
All messages are versioned, bounded, replay-protected and independently validated.
No fixed bandwidth reduction is promised; savings must be benchmarked per scene and device profile.
The SFU forwarding fast path must not execute unbounded inference.
Feature disabled means existing Pair-Dev and WebRTC behavior remains unchanged.
non_goals: Do not replace standard WebRTC audio/video as the mandatory transport.
Do not allow an LLM to sign contracts, distribute keys or grant permissions.
Do not trust self-reported peer capacity or reconstruction quality without observed validation.
Do not share raw media with the Hub/SFU in strict E2EE mode.
Do not make a slow participant force all other participants into the same quality mode.

target_topology.media_plane: Standard encrypted WebRTC media plus optional reference frames, semantic deltas and bounded residual chunks.
target_topology.control_plane: WebRTC DataChannel preferred; existing encrypted Hub Relay fallback.
target_topology.coordination_plane: Hub/SFU manages authenticated membership, epochs, opaque routing, lease ordering and expiry.
target_topology.compute_plane: Participant-local CPU/GPU/NPU workers; optional trusted server workers only after explicit non-strict-E2EE consent.
target_topology.audit_plane: Structured raw-media-free events for proposals, contracts, leases, quality, recovery and fallback.

milestones.title: Contracts and threat model
milestones.exit: Schemas, permissions and deterministic negotiation state machine approved.

milestones.title: Two-peer negotiation
milestones.exit: Two browsers negotiate signed task leases and safely fall back.

milestones.title: Semantic reconstruction
milestones.exit: Controlled scenes use references, deltas and residuals with measurable quality.

milestones.title: Multi-peer scheduling
milestones.exit: 3-10 peers support task masters, validators, churn and re-election.

milestones.title: AI-Snake learning
milestones.exit: Negotiation heuristics pass shadow, canary and rollback lifecycle.

milestones.title: Scale and rollout
milestones.exit: 100-viewer, E2EE, security and chaos gates pass behind feature flags.

tasks.title: Document threat model and E2EE trust boundaries
tasks.description: Define strict-E2EE, trusted-server and development profiles. Cover malicious peers, Sybil behavior, replay, forged leases, poisoned heuristics, fake capacity claims, inference leakage, traffic analysis and denial of service.
acceptance_criteria: Browser, AI-Snake, Hub, SFU, TURN and optional compute-worker trust boundaries are explicit.
Strict-E2EE states that Hub/SFU cannot inspect plaintext media or semantic payloads.
Each threat has prevention, detection, recovery and audit requirements.
LLM output is explicitly non-authoritative for permissions, keys and leases.
Metadata leakage and traffic-analysis limitations are documented.
Existing Pair-View default-deny control is named as the baseline.

tasks.title: Create versioned semantic WebRTC schemas
tasks.description: Add strict JSON Schemas for negotiation, leases, semantic frames, quality reports and recovery. Security-sensitive envelopes must reject unbounded additional properties.
acceptance_criteria: Every schema has $id, version discriminator, required fields and explicit bounds.
Epoch, sequence, expiry, peer and session identifiers are mandatory where authoritative.
Signatures and hash references never contain private keys.
Fixtures cover valid, expired, replayed, oversized and malformed messages.
Schemas validate independently from Angular and Flask implementations.
Binary residuals are referenced as bounded chunks rather than embedded without limits.

tasks.title: Extend Pair-Dev permissions with semantic compute roles
tasks.description: Add default-deny permissions for semantic media, compute contribution, validation, temporary task mastership and derived-data sharing while preserving all existing keys.
acceptance_criteria: Existing chat, view_tui, cursor, control, artifact_view and annotation behavior remains compatible.
Every new permission defaults to false.
No permission implies another permission.
Master eligibility requires compute contribution plus task-specific master permission.
Revocation invalidates offers and leases within a bounded timeout.
Backend and frontend use identical canonical keys.
Legacy clients cannot accidentally grant new permissions.

tasks.title: Implement deterministic compute-contract negotiation state machine
tasks.description: Implement offer, counteroffer, accept, reject, activate, renew, revoke, expire and fallback as a pure deterministic state machine. AI-Snake proposals must compile into this engine.
acceptance_criteria: Identical ordered inputs yield identical states and reason codes.
Duplicate, stale, out-of-order and expired messages are rejected idempotently.
A contract activates only with required permissions and signatures.
Negotiation rounds and duration are bounded.
Every transition emits a stable machine-readable reason_code.
Property tests cover reorder, duplicate, timeout, partial consent and revocation.
AI-Snake cannot bypass the engine.

tasks.title: Measure and normalize participant capabilities
tasks.description: Measure coarse browser-visible CPU timing, WebCodecs/WebGPU support, memory hints, network stats and user-configured limits without excessive fingerprinting.
acceptance_criteria: Service works when optional browser APIs are unavailable.
Capability values are coarse and privacy-preserving.
User resource caps override detected capacity.
Battery or thermal limits can disable or reduce contribution.
Advertisements expire and refresh at bounded intervals.
No benchmark runs before explicit permission.
Tests cover weak, strong, missing-API and revoked-consent clients.

tasks.title: Add session signatures, epochs and replay protection
tasks.description: Bind authoritative messages to session-scoped participant identities, epochs and non-reusable sequences using vetted platform cryptography.
acceptance_criteria: Hub can route but cannot forge participant acceptance.
Replay from an old session, epoch or sequence is rejected.
Key rotation does not expose keys to Hub/SFU.
Lost local state triggers safe renegotiation instead of accepting stale leases.
No custom cryptographic primitive is introduced.
Tests cover key rotation, reconnect, replay and tampered signatures.

tasks.title: Extend WebRTC DataChannel and opaque Hub Relay transport
tasks.description: Add typed bounded messages for capabilities, contracts, leases, semantic envelopes, reports and recovery. Prefer DataChannel and reuse the existing encrypted Hub Relay fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Existing view_payload behavior is unchanged.
Unknown versions and kinds are ignored with audit events.
Per-kind size and rate limits apply before expensive parsing.
Backpressure prevents unbounded DataChannel bufferedAmount growth.
Control and recovery messages have priority over residual chunks.
Relay retention is bounded by bytes, count and TTL.
Reconnect creates a new epoch and never silently reuses stale leases.
Hub never needs plaintext semantic content.

tasks.title: Implement task-scoped temporary master leases
tasks.description: Elect separate short-lived masters for motion estimation, geometry tracking, residual generation, validation and recovery. Use consent, observed performance, network, energy limits and reputation.
acceptance_criteria: There is no permanent global master.
Each lease contains task kind, scope, epoch, sequence range and expiry.
Scheduler supports primary, validators and hot standby.
Conflicting overlapping authority is rejected.
Departure, timeout, quality regression and permission revocation trigger deterministic re-election.
Equal-score ties resolve deterministically.
Clients locally reject leases exceeding their advertised limits.
Self-reported capacity alone cannot win election.

tasks.title: Add participant compute-contract configuration UI
tasks.description: Expose compute contribution, duty cycle, battery policy, permitted roles, derived-data policy and maximum reconstruction delay from 2 to 20 seconds per participant.
acceptance_criteria: Delay is configurable from 2000 to 20000 ms.
UI explains that audio and urgent interaction remain low latency.
Profiles include off, conservative, balanced and custom.
Consent changes produce a new contract epoch.
Current master, validators and lease expiry are visible.
Measured values, peer claims and deterministic decisions are visually distinguished.
Controls are keyboard accessible and usable on 5-inch and 15-inch displays.

tasks.title: Integrate AI-Snake explanations and contract proposals
tasks.description: AI-Snake explains current offers, bottlenecks and master choices. Free-text requests compile to deterministic proposals but never become authoritative without policy validation and participant consent.
acceptance_criteria: AI-Snake summarizes active contracts without exposing secrets.
Every proposal shows exact fields before acceptance.
Free text compiles into schema-valid proposal data.
AI-Snake cannot sign, grant permissions or distribute keys.
Rejected proposals return reason codes and safe alternatives.
Explanations identify uncertainty around unverified capability claims.
Master changes are explained per task rather than as one global role.

tasks.title: Register semantic settings in the existing AI-Snake config system
tasks.description: Add schema-controlled settings for enablement, governance mode, default delay, compute cap, strict E2EE, fallback mode, heuristic learning and audit verbosity.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown settings remain rejected by the existing PATCH behavior.
Defaults are conservative: feature off and compute contribution off.
Reconstruction delay is bounded to 2000-20000 ms.
Global defaults stay separate from live-session overrides.
Options endpoint exposes allowed values.
Existing AI-Snake configuration tests continue to pass.

tasks.title: Create pluggable semantic capture and heuristic pipeline
tasks.description: Represent reference frames, static background, tracked regions, geometry, UI/text primitives, motion and residuals. Deterministic geometry/change detection is primary; optional local models are secondary.
acceptance_criteria: Scene model is renderer- and model-independent.
Raw frames have explicit ownership and release lifecycle.
Sensitive regions can be excluded before processing.
Pipeline works without an LLM.
Each stage reports runtime, confidence and estimated byte savings.
Late stages are cancelled by deadlines.
Invalid model output is rejected by deterministic bounds.
Failure degrades to residual tiles or ordinary WebRTC.
Observe-only mode measures without altering media.

tasks.title: Implement semantic frame packetization and bounded residual chunks
tasks.description: Encode reference frames plus semantic deltas and bounded residual tiles. Reuse WebCodecs or standard image/video codecs for payloads rather than inventing unsafe raw compression.
acceptance_criteria: Every sequence references an available base frame or requests recovery.
Residual chunks have hashes, ordering, byte limits and expiry.
Reference frames can be forced by policy or recovery.
Packetization respects transport backpressure and message priority.
Missing chunks cannot create unbounded retention.
Malformed references fail closed and request recovery.
Synthetic deterministic fixtures cover static UI, motion and scene cut.

tasks.title: Implement client reconstruction and self-healing for 2-20 seconds
tasks.description: Reconstruct from references, geometry/motion deltas and residuals. Use the participant-specific 2-20 second window for prediction and repair, with immediate quality-triggered fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Window is negotiated per receiver rather than globally assumed.
Visual drift, stale regions and missing references are measured continuously.
Region repair is attempted before full reference refresh when safe.
Audio and urgent controls are never blocked by reconstruction.
Threshold or deadline breach requests reference frame or ordinary stream.
Recovery handles duplicate and reordered packets idempotently.
Memory is bounded by resolution, chunk caps and configured window.
A 20-second setting does not permit displaying indefinitely incorrect content.

tasks.title: Add quality metrics, validators and peer reliability
tasks.description: Measure reconstruction error, correction cost, bitrate, compute time and fallback rate. Validate master output using receiver checks, deterministic constraints and independently leased validators.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics separate sender, master, validator and receiver costs.
Strict-E2EE reports contain metrics and hashes, not raw frames.
Validation quorum adapts to session size.
Conflicts cause safe fallback rather than arbitrary acceptance.
Repeatedly wrong or late peers lose task eligibility without losing baseline call access.
Default reputation is session-scoped.
Long-term reputation requires explicit opt-in, export and deletion.
No success claim relies only on peer self-report.

tasks.title: Apply AI-Snake heuristic evolution to negotiation and scheduling
tasks.description: Reuse observation, candidate fingerprinting, validation, simulation, shadow run, 10/50/100 rollout, watchdog, quarantine and rollback for contract and scheduler heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Learned heuristics cannot alter cryptographic or permission invariants.
Candidates are fingerprinted, rate-limited, TTL-bound and quarantinable.
Shadow mode compares decisions without changing active contracts.
Activation score includes quality, bandwidth, compute, fairness and fallback effects.
Rollback triggers include drift, fallback increase, lease churn, energy-limit breach and negative feedback.
Observe-only and frozen governance modes match existing AI-Snake semantics.
Previous active heuristic is recoverable after rollback.

tasks.title: Separate SFU fast path and add automatic ordinary-video fallback
tasks.description: Keep RTP forwarding independent from negotiation and compute. Run ordinary encrypted WebRTC as baseline/fallback and switch using quality, congestion, churn and deadline gates.
acceptance_criteria: SFU forwarding loop performs no unbounded inference.
Coordinator failure does not terminate ordinary media.
Strict-E2EE disables plaintext server compute.
Trusted server compute requires explicit visible consent.
Fallback exists before semantic mode activates.
Hysteresis prevents rapid mode oscillation.
Scene cuts, high noise, excessive motion, lease loss or drift can trigger fallback.
User can force ordinary video at any time.
Returning to semantic mode requires recovery gates.

tasks.title: Extend Pair-Dev to authenticated multi-participant semantic groups
tasks.description: Add semantic negotiation groups while preserving existing two-user Pair-Dev. Membership changes create a new epoch and invalidate incompatible leases.
acceptance_criteria: Two-peer Pair-Dev is unchanged when feature is off.
Join, leave, reconnect and permission changes update epoch deterministically.
Late joiners receive current signed contract and required references.
Quorum rules adapt to participant count.
A weak client may receive ordinary fallback without forcing the whole group to fallback.
Membership authority comes from authenticated share-session state.
Peer claims cannot add members or roles.
Task leases are re-evaluated after membership changes.

tasks.title: Create simulator, browser E2E tests and 100-viewer benchmarks
tasks.description: Test deterministic network/peer simulations, real browsers and reproducible bandwidth-quality-compute comparisons against standard WebRTC.
acceptance_criteria: Seeded simulations are reproducible for 2, 3, 10 and 100 participants.
Scenarios include master crash, partition, replay, lying capability, colluding validators, scene cut and residual loss.
Two-browser E2E negotiates, leases, reconstructs, revokes and falls back.
Group E2E uses at least four mixed-capability peers.
Tests cover 2, 10 and 20 second receiver windows.
Benchmarks report average, p95 and worst observed burst.
100-viewer server egress separates SFU media, audio and Hub control traffic.
Baseline uses identical source resolution, frame rate and network conditions.
Savings are reported by scene class and device profile.
Controlled scenes may target 80-95% reduction, but worst-case acceptance is safe fallback rather than forced savings.
Quality thresholds must pass before savings count as successful.

tasks.title: Add security tests, audit UI, feature flags and rollout documentation
tasks.description: Emit raw-media-free audit events, prove strict-E2EE opacity, test abuse cases and ship behind observe-only, shadow, canary and active gates disabled by default.
acceptance_criteria: Audit contains no raw frames, residual payloads, keys or prompts.
Events include correlation ID, epoch, task kind, lease and reason code.
Debug UI shows active contract, roles, quality, bitrate, recovery and fallback.
Hub/SFU fixtures cannot decrypt strict-E2EE payloads.
Unauthorized or revoked peers cannot become master or validator.
Oversized and decompression-bomb-like inputs are rejected before large allocation.
Malformed model output cannot escape schema and policy validation.
Feature is disabled by default.
Flags independently control negotiation, semantic encoding, peer compute, trusted server compute and heuristic learning.
Automatic rollback disables semantic mode without ending the call.
Version incompatibility gracefully falls back.
Documentation explains that 2-20 seconds is reconstruction tolerance, not conversational latency.
All documented settings and paths exist after implementation.

global_acceptance_criteria: Feature disabled preserves all existing Pair-Dev, chat, permission and ordinary WebRTC behavior.
No LLM or learned heuristic can grant permissions, distribute keys, activate contracts or issue authoritative leases.
Strict-E2EE keeps plaintext media and semantic payloads inaccessible to Hub/SFU/TURN.
Every participant can cap or refuse compute and force ordinary encrypted video.
Per-participant 2-20 second reconstruction windows never delay audio or urgent controls.
Masters are short-lived, task-scoped, validated and replaced on expiry, failure, revocation or quality regression.
Mixed-capability groups can use different modes per receiver.
Bandwidth savings are measured against a standard-codec baseline with quality gates.
100-viewer tests report average and burst server egress including audio and recovery peaks.
Security tests cover replay, forged claims, stale epochs, malicious masters, validator conflict, oversized messages and heuristic poisoning.
AI-Snake heuristics use validation, simulation, shadow run, progressive rollout, quarantine and rollback.
All schemas, settings, messages, reason codes and audit events are versioned and documented.
